content.thinking: Moving v2 before publishing, matching what release.yml does. That's done — the draft URL is the untagged one, and the real URL becomes releases/tag/v2.5.1 once published.

content.text:
I upgraded pit and released pi-action 2.5.1 as a patch. The release is still a draft, so you need to review and publish it at https://github.com/cv/pi-action/releases.

The tag push did not start `release.yml`. No run appeared after several minutes, even though the v2.5.0 tag push by the same bot did start it. I couldn't push the tag again, because a repository rule blocks deleting tags. So I did the workflow's last two steps by hand:
- **Draft release:** I created the `v2.5.1` draft with the notes from #79 and the Full Changelog link.
- **Major tag:** I moved `v2` to `0c28cb8`. Users on `cv/pi-action@v2` already get 2.5.1, before you publish the draft.

The workflow's own `npm run check` step did not run for the tag. CI passed on both PRs and on `main` at that commit, which is the same command.

**What I merged:**
1. **#78 `ci: run pi-assistant with pit 0.36.3`:** this moves `.github/workflows/pi-assistant.yml` and the examples in `docs/extensions.md` from pit `v0.36.2` to `v0.36.3`. That pit release decodes JSON string literal params (cv/pit#369).
2. **#79 `chore: release 2.5.1`:** this sets the version to 2.5.1 in `package.json` and `package-lock.json`. The PR's release notes have one item under **Fixed**: a run that the agent starts inside a run now stops at once (#76). The pit upgrade only affects this repository's CI, so it has no release note.

I put an annotated `v2.5.1` tag on the merge commit `0c28cb8` on `main`. Its version matches `package.json` and `package-lock.json`.
